ops.title: Documented legacy-state remedy silently drops pack registrations, leaving heal a no-op and the binary unpatched
ops.description:
cc-patch's own remedy for a legacy state document destroys pack registrations, and nothing tells the user. The machine then reports healthy while sitting unpatched across a Claude upgrade.

## What the binary tells you to do

cc-patch 0.12.1 diagnoses a pre-v0.5.0 state document and prints its own remedy (observed in ~/Library/Logs/cc-patch/watch.log and heal.log on yasyf's Mac):

    cc-patch: parse state "~/.local/share/cc-patch/state.json": json: unknown field "overrides"
    cc-patch: state "~/.local/share/cc-patch/state.json": legacy pre-v0.5.0 state document; delete the file and re-run `cc-patch heal --all` so overrides re-derive

## What actually happens

state.json holds the pack REGISTRATIONS, not just the derived overrides. Deleting it deletes the list of installed packs. `heal --all` then has nothing registered to iterate, so it exits 0 having done nothing — a silent no-op that reads as success.

Observed on this machine (2026-07-25):

- state.json was deleted at 00:48, following the printed remedy.
- `cc-patch list` afterwards reported only "Available builtins (install by name): fastmode, tasktools" — zero installed packs.
- `cc-patch status` reported only `claude 2.1.220`, with no patch rows at all.
- `cc-patch apply --all` and `cc-patch heal --all` both exited 0 with no output and no error.
- Both launchd jobs (com.yasyf.cc-patch.watch, com.yasyf.cc-patch.heal) ran to completion with exit status 0.

Every health signal was green while the machine was unpatched.

## Why it matters

`fastmode/delegated-agents` and `tasktools/session-tasks` had been applied to Claude 2.1.218. Claude then updated 2.1.218 -> 2.1.220. Because the registrations were gone, the watch job's `apply --all` had nothing to re-apply, so 2.1.220 was never patched and fast mode for delegated agents was silently off. The upgrade-triggered watch job is precisely the mechanism meant to prevent this, and it cannot fire without registrations.

The failure is silent in both directions: the remedy does not warn that registrations are lost, and the post-remedy state reports success rather than "no packs installed".

## Repair that worked

    cc-patch install fastmode --yes
    cc-patch install tasktools --yes
    cc-patch apply --all

`install` alone was not sufficient — after both installs, `cc-patch status` still read `not patched` for both packs, and an explicit `apply --all` was required to patch 2.1.220. Worth checking whether `install` is supposed to auto-apply: the confirmation prompt it shows says "Install and auto-apply these patches?", which does not match the observed behavior.

## Suggested fix

Either make the legacy-state path preserve registrations while discarding only the stale derived overrides, or change the remedy text to say that packs must be re-installed afterwards and name the commands. Additionally, `heal --all` and `apply --all` finding zero registered packs should say so on stderr rather than exiting 0 silently, so an unpatched machine is not indistinguishable from a healthy one.

ops.text: Deleting a legacy state.json and running 'cc-patch heal --all' either preserves pack registrations or the remedy text tells the user to re-install packs
A machine whose state.json was removed cannot silently cross a Claude version upgrade unpatched
